rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، الضحاك، قتادة
rows.claim: They identify the pair as the Day of Sacrifice and the odd as the Day of Arafah; al-Dahhak says these days are singled out for their merit.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: الوتر: يوم عرفة، والشفع: يوم الذبح

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view takes the pair as the two days after the Sacrifice and the odd as the third day.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: {الشفع} [الفجر: 3] : اليومان بعد يوم النحر، {والوتر} [الفجر: 3] : اليوم الثالث

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: The pair are the two days after the Sacrifice and the odd is the later departure day, as in the choice to depart in two days or remain longer.
rows.anchor: {الشفع} [الفجر: 3] : يومان بعد يوم النحر، {والوتر} [الفجر: 3] : يوم النفر الآخر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، أبو صالح
rows.claim: All created things are paired, while God alone is one and self-sufficient; Mujahid lists paired opposites and cites creation in pairs.
rows.anchor: كل خلق الله شفع، السماء والأرض، والبر والبحر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A further gloss identifies the pair with the dawn prayer and the odd with the sunset prayer.
rows.anchor: ويقال الشفع صلاة الغداة، والوتر صلاة المغرب

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the oath as covering creation, since all creation includes what is paired and what is odd.
rows.anchor: عني بذلك الخلق، وذلك أن الخلق كله شفع ووتر

rows.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن
rows.claim: Creation as a whole is both paired and odd; al-Hasan adds that everything God made has both qualities, so the oath encompasses all creation and the visible and unseen.
rows.anchor: الخلق كله شفع ووتر، وأقسم بالخلق

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين، النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet identifies the pair and odd with prayer, since prayer contains both even and odd units.
rows.anchor: هي الصلاة منها شفع ومنها وتر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the pair and odd as number, and the report from Jabir says the pair is two days and the odd is one day.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: هو العدد

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن جابر
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that the pair means the two days and the odd the single day.
rows.anchor: الشفع: اليومان، والوتر: اليوم الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is general: without revelation or rational proof restricting it, every pair and every odd thing described by the interpreters falls within it.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكره أقسم بالشفع والوتر، ولم يخصص نوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two readings of al-watr are both widely attested in regional recitation and both are familiar Arabic dialect forms, so either is correct.
rows.anchor: فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night is described as it travels away and passes; this is the usual Arabic sense of the verb.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {والليل إذا يسر} [الفجر: 4] قال: إذا سار

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير، ابن عباس، مجاهد، أبو العالية، قتادة، ابن زيد
rows.claim: These interpreters gloss the night as moving, going, or passing away.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {والليل إذا يسر} [الفجر: 4] يقول: إذا ذهب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A distinct interpretation identifies the night with the night at Muzdalifah.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ، {والليل إذا يسر} [الفجر: 4] قال: ليلة جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers omitting the final yāʾ because it matches the rhyme of the verse endings; Arabic can drop this yāʾ in a raised form when the preceding kasra indicates it.
rows.anchor: وحذف الياء في ذلك أعجب إلينا، ليوفق بين رءوس الآي

rows.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
rows.claim: A line of poetry illustrates the Arabic omission of the yāʾ in a raised verb form.
rows.anchor: ليس تخفى يسارتي قدر يوم … ولقد تخف شيمتي إعساري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by these matters is sufficient for a discerning person who understands the Lord; it is enough without resort to weightier oaths.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {لذي حجر} [الفجر: 5] قال: لذي النهى والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person of ḥijr is one with reason and self-restraint; the word also describes a ruler's restraint placed on someone's property.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، {هل في ذلك قسم لذي حجر} [الفجر: 5] قال: لذي حلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: The reported glosses define ḥijr as reason, discernment, intelligence, or forbearance.
rows.anchor: لذي النهى والعقل

rows.speaker: قتادة، ابن زيد
rows.claim: They gloss the phrase as applying to a person of reason and intelligence; Ibn Zayd equates reason and inner understanding while noting their different Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: لذي حجى، لذي عقل ولب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings Hell on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال: جيء بها تقاد بسبعين ألف زمام، مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود، أبو وائل
rows.claim: Hell is brought led by seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: تقـاد بسبعين ألف زمام، مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He describes Paradise and the Fire at the two sides, and says this is when God descends from His Throne to His Footstool to judge creation.
rows.anchor: هذا حين ينزل من عرشه إلى كرسيه، لحساب خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day a person recalls his neglect in worldly obedience to God and good works, but is too late to benefit from the reminder.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأنى له الذكرى} [الفجر: 23] يقول: وكيف له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains the question as asking how remembrance can help the person then.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأنى له الذكرى} [الفجر: 23] يقول: وكيف له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse is the answer to the preceding oath.
rows.anchor: قال: وقع هاهنا القسم {لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد} [البلد: 4]

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، قتادة، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، مجاهد
rows.claim: One interpretation is that human beings were created amid hardship and toil, facing the burdens of worldly life and the hereafter; reports add the strain of teeth emerging.
rows.anchor: حين خلق في مشقة لا يلقى ابن آدم إلا مكابد أمر الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says no creature has to endure what the human being endures.
rows.anchor: لم يخلق الله خلقا يكابد ما يكابد ابن آدم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عكرمة، إبراهيم، عبد الله بن شداد، أبو صالح، الضحاك
rows.claim: A second interpretation understands the phrase as the human being's upright, balanced stature, standing on two legs unlike other animals.
rows.anchor: خلق منتصبا على رجلين، لم تخلق دابة على خلقه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also glosses the phrase as being on an uphill ascent.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {لقد خلقنا الإنسان في كبد} [البلد: 4] قال: في صعد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd proposes that the human being was created in the sky, which he calls al-kabad.
rows.anchor: قال: في السماء، يسمى ذلك الكبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strongest interpretation is that people were created to struggle through affairs: hardship is the established Arabic meaning of kabad, as Labid's verse illustrates.
rows.anchor: معنى ذلك أنه خلق يكابد الأمور ويعالجها

rows.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة
rows.claim: Labid's line uses the word kabad in the sense of hardship or distress, supporting the preferred interpretation.
rows.anchor: قمنا وقام الخصوم في كبد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: A day of masghabah is a day of famine or hunger.
rows.anchor: {في يوم ذي مسغبة} [البلد: 14] قال: مجاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God swears by the sun and its daytime; its manifest light is the day.
rows.anchor: أقسم جل ثناؤه بالشمس ونهارها، لأن ضوء الشمس الظاهرة هو النهار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah takes the sun's ḍuḥā as the whole daytime.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {والشمس وضحاها} [الشمس: 1] قال: هذا النهار

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the sun's ḍuḥā as its light.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {والشمس وضحاها} [الشمس: 1] قال: ضوئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun during the first half of the month, rising after the sun sets.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {والقمر إذا تلاها} [الشمس: 2] يعني: الشمس إذا تبعها القمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، قتادة
rows.claim: The reported explanations say the moon follows the day or sun, especially when the new crescent appears after sunset.
rows.anchor: يتلوها صبيحة الهلال فإذا سقطت الشمس رؤي الهلال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd describes the full cycle: the moon follows the sun in the first half of the month, then leads it in the second half.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قول الله: {والشمس وضحاها والقمر إذا تلاها} [الشمس: 2] قال: هذا قسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says daytime makes the sun apparent; although the alternative grammatical reading has a rationale, he prefers the explanation reported by the early authorities.
rows.anchor: والصواب عندنا في ذلك: ما قاله أهل العلم الذين حكينا قولهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says daytime covers the sun.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {والنهار إذا جلاها} [الشمس: 3] قال: إذا غشيها النهار

rows.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
rows.claim: Some grammarians take the pronoun to refer to darkness: daytime reveals the darkness, with a feminine pronoun for an understood, previously unmentioned referent.
rows.anchor: والنهار إذا جلا الظلمة، ويجعل الهاء والألف من جلاها كناية عن الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night covers the sun until it sets and the horizons become dark; Qatadah gives the same gloss.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {والليل إذا يغشاها} [الشمس: 4] : إذا غشاها الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the heaven and its builder, namely its Creator, who made it a roof over the earth; it can also be read as an oath by its building.
rows.anchor: والسماء ومن بناها، يعني: ومن خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ma can stand for man, as in other Quranic expressions, or the phrase can be understood as a verbal noun meaning the heaven and its building.
rows.anchor: وجائز توجيه ذلك إلى معنى المصدر، كأنه قال: والسماء وبنائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night veils the day with darkness and removes its light; the day then clears, shines, and makes visible what night concealed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {والليل إذا يغشى والنهار إذا تجلى} [الليل: 2] قال: آيتان عظيمتان يكورهما الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah calls night and day two great signs that God rotates over creation.
rows.anchor: آيتان عظيمتان يكورهما الله على الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression about creating male and female allows ma to mean the Creator or to refer to the act of creating.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يجعل ما بمعنى من، فيكون ذلك قسما من الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود، أبو الدرداء عن النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A recitation attributed to Ibn Masud and confirmed by Abu al-Darda from the Prophet reads “the male and the female,” without “and what created.”
rows.anchor: والنهار إذا تجلى والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء عن النبي ﷺ، قتادة، الحسن
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet's reading “the male and the female”; Qatadah says this occurs in some readings, while al-Hasan reads it as “and the One who created male and female.”
rows.anchor: والليل إذا يغشى والنهار إذا تجلى والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr cites Meccan usage of ma for a referent understood as a person, as grammatical support for taking the expression to mean the One who created them.
rows.anchor: وأهل مكة يقولون للرعد: سبحان ما سبحت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings' deeds differ: some disbelieve and disobey, while others believe and obey.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4] يقول: لمختلف

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah glosses the people's striving as different or varied.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4] يقول: لمختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse is the answer to the oath beginning with the night that veils.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: وقع القسم هاهنا {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4]

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah likewise says that the oath's answer occurs here.
rows.anchor: قال: وقع القسم هاهنا {إن سعيكم لشتى} [الليل: 4]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver spends in God's cause and in the ways God commanded from the wealth He bestowed, and fears God by avoiding His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فأما من أعطى واتقى} [الليل: 5] قال: أعطى ما عنده واتقى، قال: اتقى ربه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الضحاك
rows.claim: They gloss giving as giving one's available wealth or God's due, and piety as fearing God and avoiding His prohibitions; al-Dahhak adds remembering God.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {فأما من أعطى} [الليل: 5] حق الله {واتقى} [الليل: 5] محارم الله التي نهى عنها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He understands belief in al-husna as trusting that God will replace what one spends.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: وصدق بالخلف من الله

rows.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Several reports retain the interpretation that al-husna is God's promised replacement for what is spent.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، {فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: بالخلف

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن، الضحاك، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes al-husna as God's oneness and the testimony that there is no deity but God.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن، {وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: بلا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid understands al-husna as Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وصدق بالحسنى} [الليل: 6] قال: بالجنة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another reported gloss identifies al-husna with God's promise.
rows.anchor: بل معناه: وصدق بموعود الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah says the believer trusts God's good promise and acts accordingly.
rows.anchor: صدق المؤمن بموعود الله الحسن وأشبه هذه الأقوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers belief in God's promised replacement for spending, since the preceding context concerns a giver seeking that replacement; a Prophetic report supports this reading.
rows.anchor: عني به التصديق بالخلف من الله على نفقته

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن أبي الدرداء
rows.claim: The Prophet says angels pray each day for God to replace what a spender gives and ruin what a miser withholds; the passage was revealed in connection with this.
rows.anchor: اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا، وأعط ممسكا تلفا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: A report says the verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, who freed vulnerable women converts; he told his father he sought reward with God rather than strong allies.
rows.anchor: إنما أريد، أظنه قال: ما عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari contrasts the easier course of obedience prepared for the giver with the miser who withholds the bounty given by God and considers himself independent of his Lord.
rows.anchor: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في سبيل الله، ومنع ما وهب الله له من فضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds God's bounty from commanded uses and considers himself independent of his Lord, so he does not seek to obey Him or increase in what he was given.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى ذكره: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في سبيل الله، ومنع ما وهب الله له من فضله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
rows.claim: They describe the miser as withholding his wealth, surplus, or God's due, and living as if independent of the Lord.
rows.anchor: وأما من بخل بحق الله عليه، واستغنى في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes denial of al-husna to mean denying God's promised replacement, while reporting other interpretations parallel to those for the corresponding positive phrase.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] وكذب بالخلف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة
rows.claim: They say the denier rejects God's promised replacement or good promise.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] وكذب بموعود الله الذي وعد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الضحاك
rows.claim: Another interpretation says he denies God's oneness and the testimony that there is no deity but God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] وكذب بلا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid understands the denied al-husna as Paradise.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {وكذب بالحسنى} [الليل: 9] قال: بالجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the denier for the harder course: acting in ways He dislikes and does not approve.
rows.anchor: والعسرى التي أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه ييسره لها: العمل بما يكرهه ولا يرضاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb yassara can describe sheep made ready for birth; the “harder” phrase parallels the earlier easing for the easier path even without an expressed preposition.
rows.anchor: قد يسرت غنم فلان: إذا ولدت وتهيأت للولادة

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
rows.claim: When asked whether people should rely on their written destinies, the Prophet commands them to act: each person is made ready for his path, and he recites the two contrasting passages.
rows.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن علي
rows.claim: Several versions say each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written, yet people must act; each is facilitated toward the work for which they were created.
rows.anchor: لا اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن النزال بن سبرة
rows.claim: A report says every soul's outcome is written; in response to an Arab's question the Prophet says God guides each person toward good or evil, with these verses cited.
rows.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له، فمن يرد الله به خيرا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن سعد بن عبيدة وأبي عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: When asked what work means if everything is decreed, the Prophet says to act because each person is facilitated for the easier or harder path.
rows.anchor: اعملوا فكل ميسر: سنيسره لليسرى، وسنيسره للعسرى

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses being made ready for the harder path as being made ready for evil by God.
rows.anchor: فسنيسره للعسرى} [الليل: 10] للشر من الله

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked whether people act for something already decided or begin something new, the Prophet answers that every worker is made ready for his work.
rows.anchor: كل عامل ميسر لعمله

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن بشير بن كعب
rows.claim: The Prophet says work follows what the pens and decrees have fixed, but people must still act; each is facilitated for the work for which they were created.
rows.anchor: اعملوا، فكل عامل ميسر لعمله الذي خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns the blazing Fire of Hell; people should avoid disobeying or disbelieving in God lest they enter it. The form تلظى is treated as a future verb with the extra tāʾ omitted.
rows.anchor: صلي النار التي تلظى التقي، ووضع أفعل موضع فعيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most Godfearing person will be kept from the blazing Fire; al-atqā is used with the sense of al-taqī.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وسيجنبها الأتقى} [الليل: 17] يقول: وسيوقى صلي النار التي تلظى التقي، ووضع أفعل موضع فعيل

rows.speaker: طرفة بن العبد
rows.claim: Tarafa's use of awḥad for “alone/one” supports the substitution of an afʿal form for a faʿīl form.
rows.anchor: فتلك سبيل لست فيها بأوحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by the ḍuḥā, which he takes to mean the whole daytime, based on the expression for being exposed to the sun; another view restricts it to the forenoon hour.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {والضحى} [الضحى: 1] : ساعة من ساعات النهار

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatadah takes the ḍuḥā as one of the daytime hours.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {والضحى} [الضحى: 1] : ساعة من ساعات النهار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، مجاهد، قتادة، الضحاك، ابن زيد
rows.claim: The reported glosses describe night as arriving, departing, becoming level, or settling and stilling the creatures.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {والليل إذا سجى} [الضحى: 2] قال: إذا استوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that night settle over its people and remain in darkness, like a calm sea; the root can describe stillness.
rows.anchor: والليل إذا سكن بأهله، وثبت بظلامه

rows.speaker: الأعشى، راجز
rows.claim: Poetry uses sāj for a calm sea and describes a still night, supporting the author's preferred sense of settled stillness.
rows.anchor: وبحرك ساج ما يواري الدعامصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the oath's answer: God has neither left Muhammad nor hated him; the object of “hated” is omitted because the preceding clause makes it clear.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ما ودعك ربك وما قلى} [الضحى: 3] يقول: ما تركك ربك، وما أبغضك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن زيد
rows.claim: They gloss the clauses as God not leaving or hating Muhammad; Ibn Zayd explains qālī as one who hates.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ما ودعك ربك وما قلى} [الضحى: 3] يقول: ما تركك ربك، وما أبغضك

rows.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
rows.claim: When revelation was delayed, a woman said Muhammad had been abandoned or left by Satan; God sent down the opening of the sūrah to refute the claim.
rows.anchor: أبطأ جبريل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقالت امرأة

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: One report says Khadija told the distressed Prophet that she thought his Lord had rejected him when Gabriel's revelation was delayed.
rows.anchor: ما أرى ربك إلا قد قلاك

rows.speaker: قتادة، الضحاك، ابن عباس
rows.claim: They report that Gabriel's delay led people in Mecca to say God had abandoned and hated Muhammad, prompting the verse; Ibn Abbas says the delay lasted several days.
rows.anchor: أبطأ عليه جبريل، فقال المشركون: قد قلاه ربه وودعه

rows.speaker: عروة عن عائشة
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet was deeply distressed by the delay, and Khadija reassured him that his Lord had not rejected him.
rows.anchor: فجزع جزعا شديدا، وقالت خديجة: أرى ربك قد قلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises the Prophet relief alongside the hardship of striving against the polytheists, including eventual victory and their accepting the truth willingly or under compulsion.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أبشروا أتاكم اليسر، لن يغلب عسر يسرين»

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to reassure his companions that one hardship will not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: أبشروا أتاكم اليسر، لن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says that even if hardship entered a burrow, ease would follow it, citing the repeated promise.
rows.anchor: لو دخل العسر في جحر، لجاء اليسر حتى يدخل عليه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says ease follows hardship.
rows.anchor: يسرا قال: يتبع اليسر العسر
